findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example ; policy: none, pct: 100, rua: true

findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed despite reporting; increases BEC/wire-fraud and phishing risk to customers and finance processes, and may affect cyber-insurance diligence.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject, validating all legitimate senders and alignment first.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all ; qualifier: ~all, lookup_count: 2

findings.deal_impact: Softfail weakens sender enforcement and, combined with non-enforced DMARC, leaves spoofing risk that should be remediated post-close.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders, then change SPF ~all to -all once all legitimate sources are included.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled

evidence.excerpt: queried_name: brightwaterfleet.example, record_type: DS, enabled: false

findings.deal_impact: Without DNSSEC, DNS responses lack cryptographic validation, a low-severity hygiene gap for brand and service integrity.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/registry and validate DS/DNSKEY chain and resolver handling.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: hostname: vpn.brightwaterfleet.example, pattern: vpn, first_seen: 2023-02-11, last_seen: 2026-09-30; risky_hostnames_count: 4
hostname: jenkins-old.brightwaterfleet.example, pattern: jenkins|old, first_seen: 2021-06-03, last_seen: 2026-08-14
hostname: staging-api.brightwaterfleet.example, pattern: staging, first_seen: 2024-01-20, last_seen: 2026-10-01
hostname: legacy-portal.brightwaterfleet.example, pattern: legacy, first_seen: 2019-11-05, last_seen: 2026-07-22

findings.deal_impact: Public CT names suggest VPN, legacy CI, staging and legacy portal exposure; requires validation of access controls, patching and whether systems are still needed.

remediation.summary: Inventory and validate each risky hostname; decommission legacy/staging systems or restrict them behind authenticated access.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size
findings.deal_impact: 47 unique hostnames for a 201-1000 employee company suggests attack-surface sprawl and asset-inventory gaps to confirm in diligence.

remediation.summary: Reconcile all 47 CT hostnames to owners and business need; remove or consolidate unowned/stale services.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support: TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true, TLSv1.3: not_tested; tls_versions: [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2]

findings.deal_impact: Deprecated TLS on www weakens transport security and may fail customer, compliance and insurer baseline requirements.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1, retaining TLSv1.2+ with modern cipher configuration.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: headers: strict-transport-security: null, content-security-policy: null, x-frame-options: SAMEORIGIN, server: nginx
headers: strict-transport-security: null, content-security-policy: null, x-frame-options: null

findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS allows downgrade to insecure HTTP on first visits, a low-severity but easily remediated web hygiene issue.

remediation.summary: Set Strict-Transport-Security with an appropriate max-age on apex and www after confirming all subdomains support HTTPS.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, vendor: ExampleGate, product: ExampleGate SSL-VPN, version: 7.0.11, match_level: product, match_tier: appliance_exposed, note: KEV lists products, not affected versions; version not verified.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure to a known-exploited internet-facing SSL-VPN appliance; version not verified, so urgent patch/compensating-control confirmation is a pre-close diligence priority.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify ExampleGate version and patch status against KEV entry; patch, upgrade or restrict appliance access and hunt for compromise.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: type: state_ag_breach_notice, date: 2025-08-14, summary: Notice filed for unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. disclosed_within_months: 14, entity_match: exact

findings.deal_impact: Recent disclosed breach (14 months ago, ~3,100 notified) raises residual notification, regulatory, litigation and remediation-cost questions for underwriting and purchase agreement protections.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident report, regulator correspondence and closure evidence; confirm remediation, notification completion and any ongoing obligations.

deal_recommendations.text: Make signing contingent on verification of the appliance version and patch status and a compromise assessment in Days 0–30, and obtain the current SOC 2 Type II report and a management security interview before relying on this rating [F-008].
Include a scoped review of the known-exploited appliance exposure, covering version, patching, access restrictions and compromise hunting, in Days 0–30 [F-008].
Secure protection for pre-closing incident losses, including notification, regulatory and litigation obligations arising from the disclosed incident, with remediation confirmed in Days 31–60 [F-009].

Assume the known incident is likely to be excluded from representations and warranties coverage and confirm the position with the broker before close, using closure evidence obtained in Days 31–60 [F-009].
Confirm insurability and any underwriting requirements arising from non-enforced DMARC before close, with enforcement moved to quarantine then reject in Days 31–60 [F-001].

Commit to completing remediation after close, covering DMARC and SPF enforcement, hostname validation, removal of deprecated TLS and incident obligations across Days 31–60 and Days 61–100 [F-001] [F-002] [F-004] [F-006] [F-009].

No price adjustment is warranted on cyber remediation alone: the $80K–$388K total across Days 0–30 through After day 100 is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band [F-001] [F-002] [F-003] [F-004] [F-005] [F-006] [F-007] [F-008] [F-009].

narrative.executive_summary: Bottom line: Escalate: full cyber diligence required before signing. The 71.6 rating of C reflects a critical, potentially exploitable exposure, a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months, and limited evidence: outside-in signals only [F-008] [F-009]. Key risks: Critical internet-facing appliance exposure with version not verified, non-enforced DMARC enabling spoofing, exposed admin, legacy and staging hostnames, and a disclosed incident with 3,100 individuals notified; no SOC 2 report was provided [F-008] [F-001] [F-004] [F-009]. Management credibility: Not assessed: no management interview provided. Next steps: Complete diligence before signing, verify the appliance version, patch status and compromise assessment, obtain incident closure evidence, and request the SOC 2 report that was not provided, plus a management security interview [F-008] [F-009].

Provide the incident report, regulator correspondence and closure evidence, including confirmation of notification completion and any ongoing obligations [F-009]?

Provide the plan to move DMARC from reporting to quarantine then reject and to change SPF to hard fail after validating legitimate senders [F-001] [F-002]?
